title: Clinical and exercise professional opinion on designing a postpartum return-to-running training programme: an international Delphi study and consensus statement
authors: Deering RE, Donnelly GM, Brockwell E, Bo K, Davenport MH, De Vivo M, Dufour S, Forner L, Mills H, Moore IS, Olson A, Christopher SM
population: Clinical and exercise professionals working with postpartum runners (3-round Delphi: 118, 107 and 95 participants)
findings: Consensus (at least 75% agreement) reached on 42 of 47 statements (89%).

Recommendations include a period of relative rest, gradual increases in duration and intensity, a walk-run protocol start, and incorporating strength training; an individualised prescription is emphasised.
Training should be modified for musculoskeletal or pelvic symptoms, sleep, mental health, lactation or energy availability concerns.
Cost of and access to experienced postpartum running professionals were identified as barriers.
limitations: Expert opinion, not outcome data; no specific return week, load numbers or injury-reduction evidence. Goom 2019 guidelines are grey literature and were not verified.
implications: Add a postpartum mode with no default time-based return date; start with walk-run, increase duration before intensity, include strength training (2 or more sessions/week is a design default), and make progression conditional on no pelvic floor symptoms or pain.
Add check-ins (sleep, mood, lactation, energy availability, pelvic symptoms) that can pause progression; refer symptoms to a pelvic health professional rather than adjusting around them.
Label any numeric week thresholds as common clinical practice, not research findings.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (BJSM, 2024-01, Deering). Europe PMC abstract (PMID 38191239) supports findings. Evidence level lowered A to D because the data are structured expert opinion; added the abstract's 'individualised exercise prescription' emphasis.
